search.query: how can I tell if a flood photo is current?
search.answer: Look for older copies of the photo first. If it was online before the flood, it isn't current.
voice.transcript: Panel 3: slight lifting of paint at the lower left corner.
doc.long: Bid A totals $48,200 for roof replacement, including tear-off,
underlayment, flashing and five-year labor warranty. Bid B totals
$39,900 for the same scope. Bid B's line items omit the repair of
the rotted fascia along the north wall noted in the inspection.
The inspection estimates that repair at $6,800 to $9,400. Bid B
also excludes disposal fees, listed in Bid A at $1,150. Adjusted
for these two omissions, Bid B rises to between $47,850 and
$50,450. Both contractors are licensed and insured. Bid A can
start in three weeks; Bid B in five. The board asked for a
recommendation before the March meeting, with any revised bids
attached. Staff recommend requesting revised bids from both
contractors that include the fascia repair and disposal, so the
comparison is like for like. The current low bid is not the
lowest once the omitted work is added. Next step: send the
inspection report to both contractors with a two-week deadline.
doc.summary:
Cheaper bid leaves out the repair cost.
Revise both bids.
